harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Built a fresh 3-member MariaDB Galera cluster on node1/node2/node3 (MariaDB 10.5.29 + Galera 26.4.22, RHEL9) since no database software existed on the nodes beforehand. Configured wsrep on all nodes (fixing an alphabetical config-include bug where a custom galera-cluster.cnf was silently overridden by the default galera.cnf's wsrep_on=0), opened firewalld ports, bootstrapped the cluster, and loaded an application table (appdb.orders, 4 committed rows, qty_total=42) replicated to all three nodes. Performed the full maintenance-window shutdown (stopped node3, then node2, then node1 last so it retained the highest seqno / safe_to_bootstrap=1), confirmed the cluster was completely down (all three mariadb services inactive), then brought it back (galera_new_cluster on node1, node2 and node3 rejoined via SST) with all committed rows verified present and all three members reporting wsrep_cluster_size=3 / Synced. Additionally ran the mandatory one-node-at-a-time restart protocol via systemctl reboot on all three nodes, proving a changed boot_id on each and full cluster/data recovery after each individual restart, never taking down more than one node concurrently during that phase.
actions_performed: Discovered no MariaDB/Galera packages were installed on node1/node2/node3 (fresh RHEL 9.8 nodes)
Installed mariadb-server, mariadb-server-galera, mariadb-backup, galera on all three nodes via dnf
Added CLUSTER_HOSTS entries to /etc/hosts on all nodes; opened firewalld ports 3306,4444,4567(tcp/udp),4568 on all nodes; confirmed SELinux mysqld_port_t already covers Galera ports

Diagnosed and fixed a config-precedence bug (galera-cluster.cnf overridden by default galera.cnf's wsrep_on=0 due to alphabetical include order) by editing /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf directly with wsrep_on=ON, cluster name, gcomm address, and per-node wsrep_node_address/name
Bootstrapped node1 with galera_new_cluster, then started mariadb on node2 and node3 which joined via rsync SST, reaching wsrep_cluster_size=3 and Synced on all nodes
Created appdb.orders table and inserted 4 rows, verifying replication to all three nodes; enabled mariadb systemd unit on all nodes for boot persistence

Performed full cluster shutdown for the maintenance window: stopped node3, node2, then node1 (last), confirming grastate.dat seqno ordering (7,8,9) and safe_to_bootstrap=1 on node1; confirmed all three mariadb services inactive

Brought the cluster back: galera_new_cluster on node1 (verified data intact), then started node2 and node3 which rejoined via SST; verified wsrep_cluster_size=3, Synced, and all 4 committed rows present on every node
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline on all three nodes
Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, confirmed mariadb active with wsrep_cluster_size=3/Synced and data intact before proceeding
Restarted node2 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, confirmed mariadb active with wsrep_cluster_size=3/Synced and data intact before proceeding
Restarted node3 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, confirmed mariadb active with wsrep_cluster_size=3/Synced and data intact
Final cross-check on node1: wsrep_cluster_size=3, Synced, wsrep_incoming_addresses lists all three node IPs, rows_total=4, qty_total=42
